svg.title: Defence in depth: six rings between untrusted code and the outside, and who provides each control
svg.text: Sandbox, platform and public blocks; sandbox nodes sit in their own security group
That group admits only the cluster group, and the cluster group admits it back
No public IP on any node; one shared route table sends outbound traffic to the NAT gateway
2 Access to the cluster and to AWS (identity level)
API endpoint open only to the admin address; API-only authentication
Cluster, platform-node and sandbox-node IAM roles with managed minimal policies, no inline ones
Control-plane audit and authenticator logs go to CloudWatch for 7 days
Own node pool, node class, subnets, security group and role; a taint keeps every other pod off
Metadata service needs IMDSv2 with a hop limit of 1
4 Kubernetes policy (admission, identity and pod-network level)
Pod Security 'restricted' on every namespace; quota and limits on the sandbox namespace
Minimal RBAC for the Manager and Router; the sandbox service account has no role
Default-deny network policy: a sandbox reaches only the gateway on port 3128, only the router reaches it
The cluster's network-policy agent enforces it (EKS Auto Mode ships it switched off; we turn it on)
Gateway pods can reach three internet domain names and nothing else (a domain-name policy)
One microVM with its own kernel per pod (Nitro Sandboxes); its metadata address gives placement data only
Every template names the isolated runtime class
Non-root, read-only root, no capabilities, default seccomp, no service-account token
The environment holds a placeholder, never a secret
On the one way out (application level)
Gateway: allowlist per session, rate limit,
byte budget, TLS ended for one host only
Broker: credentials of 15 minutes at most,
checked by the API for signature and expiry
20 calls a minute, token ends with the session
Every service: one audit line per event
An ingress network policy on every service
names who may call it, and on which port
an AWS service or built-in behaviour
a Kubernetes feature that we configured
our design: a choice we made or code we wrote
Platform pods have no egress network policy,
Routing is one shared table for both kinds
The sandbox group admits all traffic from the
cluster group; pod policies narrow it.
